html:
Anandamath is a Bengali novel by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, published in 1882. Its song "Vande Mataram", "I bow to thee, Mother", became the rallying cry of the Indian freedom movement.

The story is set in Bengal in the 1770s, during the famine of 1770 and the Sannyasi rebellion, when bands of wandering ascetics fought the Company and the nawab's forces. In the novel a band of monks, the "children", vow to serve the motherland, pictured as a goddess, and fight the Muslim ruler of Bengal.

The song, written a few years before the novel, praises Bengal as a mother and goddess. During the protests against the Partition of Bengal in 1905 it was sung across India. In 1950 India adopted it as its national song, beside the anthem.

The book is also divisive. Its villains are Muslim rulers, and it ends by accepting British rule as a stage before Hindu revival. For this many Muslims objected to the song, and critics see the novel as an early source of Hindu nationalism. It remains a key text of the Bengal Renaissance.
sum: Anandamath is a Bengali novel by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay, published in 1882. Its song "Vande Mataram", "I bow to thee, Mother", became the rallying cry of the Indian freedom movement.
